service.description: A party as the current user may see it (the entity filters, and a personal contact only its owner's) and what the user may do with it. With need (view, edit or delete) an error when the user may not; a party the user may not see is "not found". Who may change a directory party (canEdit, need edit): a contact admin. Who may change its identity and channels alone (canEditIdentity, need identity: the names, emails, phones, websites and addresses), besides them: (Sales owner contract, impl-sales P3 review and P4, F98; the user's calls of Nov 13, 2026) a holder of SALES_ACCOUNT_EDIT for a person owned by an organization of their sales scope (never a shared, _NA_, person) who is a current contact of an account owned by an organization of the scope (mantle/sales/SalesAccess.js contactAccounts, not a shared account) and has no user account (isSalesEditor); never the organizations, relationships, notes, photo or delete, which stay canEdit's.

parameter.name: need
parameter.description: view, edit or delete; empty only reports

parameter.name: canEditIdentity
parameter.description: May change the names and channels (emails, phones, websites, addresses): canEdit, or a Sales account editor of the contact (isSalesEditor)

service.description: The side list rows of the parties given, in their order, leaving out those the user may not see and the disabled (merged or deleted) ones: name, kind, organization and title (a person's current PrtContact or PrtEmployee relationship to an organization the user may see), the primary email (EmailPrimary first) and phone (PhonePrimary, then PhoneMobile, first), personal or not, a face image or not, and the star of the user's default book.

The Contacts side list for a scope, narrowed by text (name, organization, email or phone), a group of a book and a first letter, limited (a 320 px pane has no room for paging): all (the directory, the parties with a role, and the user's personal contacts: one mantle.party.PartyServices.find#Party with anyField and hasRole, whose count is exact), directory (the same without personal contacts), mine (the members of the user's personal books and the user's personal contacts), a contact book id (find#ContactBookParties, with contactBookGroupId), recent (the parties of the user's communication events of the last 90 days, the latest first) and ungrouped (the members of the user's books that are in no group of them). The rows are get#ContactRows'. The scope's book, its groups and the user's books come back for the scope selector and the chips.

parameter.name: rowCount
parameter.description: The rows found, maybe more than shown

parameter.name: contactBook
parameter.description: The book of a book scope, from get#UserContactBooks

service.description: What the contact record shows of a party the user may see (check#ContactAccess), for template/ContactRecord.xml: the names, the access, the roles, the contact information other than addresses with their purposes (the expired ones too with showExpired), the addresses, each kind's primary one first (isPrimary: the email, phone, website and address mantle.party.ContactServices.get#PartyContactInfo answers for the Primary purposes, a phone or email the primary address names included as a row of its own, read only), a person's organizations and titles, the relationships, the books and groups the party is in among the user's books, the notes, the employee directory card (organization, position, manager), and for a personal contact the books of its banner. Nothing for a party the user may not see.

parameter.name: otherBookList
parameter.description: The user's books the party is not in that the user may edit

service.description: One tab of the contact record beyond the overview, for a party the user may see: calendar (the party's events from 30 days ago to 90 days ahead, mantle.work.EventServices.get#FullCalendarData), tasks (the WetTask work efforts the party is on or linked to, while the user may see each task, open ones first) and requests (the requests the party is on). The consent tab is ironstone.comms.ConsentServices.get#ContactConsent.

The names of a contact the user may change (mantle.party.PartyServices.update#PartyDetail); a field left out is not changed, an empty one is cleared. A person needs a first or last name, an organization a name.

A person's organization and title: with partyRelationshipId the title (relationshipName) of that current PrtContact or PrtEmployee relationship; with organizationPartyId (an organization the user may see) a new PrtContact relationship, or the title of the current one to it. thruNow ends the relationship given.

A relationship of a contact the user may change to another party the user may see: the contact is the from party (the type describes it: Joe is a Contact of Acme) unless reverse; a directory party is not related to a personal contact.
A note on a contact the user may change (mantle.party.PartyNote); with noteDate the user's own note of that date is changed, or removed when noteText is empty.

An email, phone, website or address of a contact the user may change, with its purpose: new, or with contactMechId a change of that one (mantle.party.ContactServices.store#PartyContactInfo, which keeps the purpose and makes a new contact mechanism for the changed value). kind is email, phone, web or postal; a phone is digits, ten of them an area code and number, eleven starting with 1 also the country code, or countryCode, areaCode and contactNumber as given.

Adds a purpose to a current contact mechanism of a contact the user may change (store#PartyContactMech), or with remove ends that purpose (delete#PartyContactMech); without a purpose remove ends the contact mechanism.

The photo of a contact the user may change (check#ContactAccess need edit: the owner of a personal contact, a contact admin for the directory; impl R7): a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP file of at most 5 MB, stored by mantle.party.PartyServices.create#PartyContent as PcntFaceImage. It takes the place of the photo before, whose rows and files are removed (remove#ContactAvatar keepPartyContentId), as Settings/Account's own photo does.

Removes the photo of a contact the user may change (check#ContactAccess need edit): its PcntFaceImage PartyContent rows and their files under the party's content folder (a file that cannot be deleted is logged; its row is gone), but keepPartyContentId (the photo just uploaded). The initials show in its place.
The location of the latest face image of a party the user may see; null when it has none.

Puts a contact the user may see in a book the user may edit, with the groups of that book given (and out of the book's other groups), or with remove takes it out of the book (mantle.party.ContactBookServices add#ContactBookParties, remove#ContactBookGroupParties and remove#ContactBookParties check the book's permission and that a personal contact goes only in its owner's books).

The contacts given (those the user may see) or a book the user may view (with its group) as a vCard or CSV file (mantle.party.ContactImportServices.export#Contacts), written to the user's own export folder, dbresource://ironstone/ContactExport/{userId}/, for the screen to send as a download (ec.web.sendResourceResponse, which names the file from the location).

Two contacts side by side for a merge (both must be ones the user may see and change): the fields each has, the rows of the compare (label, the two values, and which differ), and whether they may be merged and which way: a directory party is never merged into a personal contact (link the personal contact to the directory instead), and an internal organization is never merged away. A pair the user may not change both of may still be merged when Mantle's merge guards admit the user for it (mantle.party.DuplicateServices.check#PartyMerge: a Sales manager or administrator for an account of their organization, impl-sales P3, F45); the guards' refusal (another organization, another kind) is the reason shown.

Merges one contact into the other the user keeps (get#ComparePair says which may be kept): the fields chosen from the other side first go on the kept one (update#PartyDetail), then mantle.party.DuplicateServices.merge#Parties moves the rest (contact information, roles, relationships, books, groups, work efforts, requests, messages) and disables the other party. A personal contact merged into a directory party is linked to the directory (link#PersonalContactToDirectory).

parameter.name: takeFields
parameter.description: Comma-separated fields to take from the other contact

service.description: The candidate duplicate pairs the last scan found (parties with hasDuplicates Y, mantle.party.DuplicateServices find#PartyDuplicates for their matches, each with its matchType), among the directory parties the user may see (the duplicate services leave personal contacts out, and they are left out here too; and the pairs marked not duplicates, mark#PartyNotDuplicate), grouped by reason: same email, same phone, same name (a similar name, with Mantle's nameScore, or the same name and birthday), same address and same identification.

parameter.name: limit
parameter.description: The most pairs of each reason

service.description: Records that two directory parties the user may see are not duplicates (contact admins, and a merger Mantle's merge guards admit for the pair, a Sales manager or administrator for accounts of their organization, impl-sales P3): mantle.party.DuplicateServices.mark#PartyNotDuplicate, after which the duplicate services and the scan leave the pair out and the parties' duplicate flags are checked again.

Once, on a data load (data/BossSetupData.xml): the "not a duplicate" decisions BOSS kept in a PartySetting of each party (BossNotDuplicates, a comma list of the other party ids) become Mantle's PartyNotDuplicate rows (one per pair, the lower id first), and the settings and their type go. A pair whose party is gone is dropped; a party whose setting fails is logged and the rest go on, its setting kept for the next load.
The draft of an import of the current user: the draft map (empty when there is none, or the id is not a draft id), the location of its file, and the folder.

actions.script: draft = {} found = false fileLocation = null const userId = ec.user.userId if (!userId || !importId || !/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,40}$/.test(String(importId))) return folder = `dbresource://ironstone/ContactImport/${userId}/${importId}` const text = ec.resource.getLocationReference(folder + '/draft.json').getText() if (!text) return try { draft = JSON.parse(text) || {} } catch (err) { ec.logger.warn(`Contact import ${importId} of ${userId}: the draft does not read: ${err}`); draft = {}; return } found = true fileLocation = draft.fileExt ? `${folder}/source.${draft.fileExt}` : null

service.description: Merges the fields given into the draft of an import of the current user and saves it.

The import's first step: the file (an upload, or the file already in the draft when none is given) read as text in its character set (mantle.party.ContactImportServices.read#ContactFileText: UTF-8, Windows-1252, ISO-8859-1, or UTF-16 with or without its byte order mark), kept as the draft's source file, and parsed (mantle.party.ContactImportServices.parse#ContactFile) for its kind, preset, columns and mapping, which start the draft. A new import gets an id; the same importId replaces its file.

The import's last step: mantle.party.ContactImportServices.import#Contacts of the draft's file with its mapping and options (each row in its own transaction: a row that fails is reported and the rest are imported), the result kept in the draft (counts, the failures with their reasons and values, the rows) for the result view and the failures download. A directory import is for contact admins. A file of up to 100 rows is imported in the request; a larger one (or background true) runs on as a job (run#ImportNow): the draft is running, the user gets the progress on the topic contactImportProgress (progressKey the importId), and the draft ends done or failed. An import running or done is not started again.

parameter.name: background
parameter.description: Run as a job; by default, a file of more than 100 rows

service.description: Imports the draft's file now (for run#Import, in the request or as its job, as the user who started it): mantle.party.ContactImportServices.import#Contacts with the progress going to the user, then the draft done with its result. An import that stops (an error before the rows, say) leaves the draft failed with the error, never running, so it can be run again.
